mismatch_patterns.explanation: The app declares multiple sensitive SMS permissions (RECEIVE_SMS, READ_SMS, SEND_SMS) in the manifest, but there is no evidence of any SMS-related API usage at runtime, nor any UI element or justification for SMS access. This may indicate permissions are planted for future malicious activation or to evade static analysis.

Location permissions (ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION) are declared in the manifest, but there is no runtime evidence of location access or any UI indication. This is suspicious as it suggests unnecessary or dormant permission requests.
Contacts permissions (READ_CONTACTS, WRITE_CONTACTS) are declared but not used at runtime and not mentioned in the UI. This could be a sign of a dormant or planned mismatch.
READ_PHONE_STATE is declared but not exercised at runtime and not justified in the UI, indicating possible future abuse.
WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared but not used at runtime and not mentioned in the UI, suggesting unnecessary or dormant permission.
INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE are declared but not used at runtime and not mentioned in the UI, which is suspicious for an app with no visible user-facing purpose.

prompt3_mismatch_detection.analyst_notes: This app declares a wide range of highly sensitive permissions but shows no user-facing purpose and no runtime use of those permissions. This is a classic sign of a dormant or staged mismatch, though no active malicious behavior is currently detected. The presence of an exported receiver component further increases the risk of future abuse. No SILENT_EXEC or UI_DECEPTION is present at this time, but the UNOBSERVED_DECLARED pattern is strong and widespread.
